records.name: Ardahan
records.current_summary: This province has no province-specific law, ordinance or incident series in the audited record; what a trans visitor here stands under is the same national framework that binds every province. A leaked draft omnibus justice package from October 2025 (the '11th Judicial Package') would enable criminal charges against LGBT people across Turkiye - Human Rights Watch called it one of the most alarming rights rollbacks in decades - and it contains no province-specific provisions. The LGBTI+ association Kaos GL reported that in 2025 anti-LGBTI+ hostility became institutionalised as state policy under a 'Year of the Family' banner, with senior officials' rhetoric and instructions to public institutions creating a climate encouraging rights violations.  Because the surviving record is entirely national-level and carries no provincial breakdown, neither a more protective nor a more hostile local regime can be established for this province; the documented national picture applies here unchanged.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch news release (29 Oct 2025) on the leaked '11th Judicial Package' draft omnibus law: would amend the Turkish penal and civil codes to criminalise behaviour deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', criminalise taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony (penalties up to 4 years in prison), raise the minimum age for gender-affirming health care including surgery from 18 to 25 with mandatory permanent infertility, and punish health professionals who perform such care - HRW calls it one of the most alarming rollbacks of LGBT rights in decades, and 15 Turkish LGBT groups plus the Turkish Medical Association oppose the draft.

Kaos GL report launch on the 2025 report 'A major siege against LGBTI+ people in 2025: Hostility turned into state policy': documents that anti-LGBTI+ hostility became institutionalised as explicit state policy, with senior officials' hate speech and instructions issued to public institutions under a 'Year of the Family' banner creating a climate that encouraged human-rights violations, and regulatory/supervisory bodies systematically restricting freedom of expression and artistic freedom; findings were presented by lawyer Kerem Dikmen at the launch.

records.name: Bitlis
records.current_summary: Every province in Türkiye sits under the same intensifying national framework. A leaked draft of the 11th Judicial Package (October 2025) would criminalise LGBT conduct and advocacy — up to 3 years for behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' and 4 years for same-sex ceremonies — and would raise gender-affirming-care eligibility from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate, exposing providers to fines and up to 7 years and patients to up to 3 years; 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected. The Kaos GL 2025 human-rights report ('A Major Siege', published February 2026) finds hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 — presidency-centred, implemented through the family ministry — documenting 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture or ill-treatment cases (up from 51) and 313 liberty violations (about 2.5-fold), counted from media coverage because the state keeps no hate-crime statistics.  No province-specific ordinance, incident series or court decision concerning trans visitors in Bitlis was documented in this research pass; the national framework above is the whole documented picture for Bitlis. The absence of recorded provincial enforcement is not evidence of local tolerance, and equally not evidence of a local ban.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch (29 October 2025): a leaked draft of Türkiye's 11th Judicial Package would amend penal-code article 225 to punish conduct 'contrary to biological sex' with up to 3 years in prison and would allow charges for anyone taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony (up to 4 years) plus, under civil-code article 40, raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate (providers facing fines and up to 7 years, patients up to 3 years); 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected and HRW calls for withdrawal. This is the national framework this province's record stands under; the article records no province-specific enforcement or incidents.

Kaos GL's LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 ('A Major Siege', published 24 February 2026) finds hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 under 'Year of the Family' instructions, documenting six right-to-life violations including three hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (up from 51), and 313 right-to-liberty violations (about 2.5 times the previous year, mostly detentions); the state keeps no official hate-crime statistics, so data rely on media coverage. It is a national-level report and contains no province-specific detail.

sources.claim: Human Rights news release (29 October 2025): the leaked 11th Judicial Package omnibus draft law would amend the penal and civil codes to criminalise conduct deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality" (up to three years), sharply restrict gender-affirming healthcare (minimum age 25, onerous eligibility conditions) and allow criminal charges against both trans people and the professionals providing their care; the government's stated justification is protecting "the family" and "public morals"; the package also carries unrelated measures such as longer child sentences and online-content removal.

Wikipedia's Turkey country overview independently corroborates and updates the national-framework claims in the Edirne record: same-sex activity has been decriminalised since the 1858 Ottoman penal code and transgender people could change legal gender from 1988, yet same-sex marriage, civil unions and domestic partnerships remain unavailable with no comprehensive anti-discrimination law, while LGBTQ people are barred from open military service. Crucially for the record's October 2025 draft-law claim, Wikipedia reports that in early 2026 Turkish media said the government was considering legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex', but that provision was ultimately not included in that year's judicial reform package. It also dates the surrounding hostility: in May 2025 Erdoğan declared a 'Decade of Family and Population' for 2026-2035 at the International Family Forum with explicit anti-LGBTI rhetoric, Pride events were repeatedly disallowed in 2024 and 2025 with police detaining participants, and the European Commission's Türkiye Report 2025 concludes the country's laws and their implementation do not properly protect LGBTQ people. The page has nothing Edirne-specific, so it functions purely as the framework document under which a visitor to Edirne stands.
